# Tobit Chapter 5 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_005_page_001.jpg

---

**5:1** Tobias answered his father: "I will do everything you have commanded me, Father.

**5:2** But how am I to receive the money from him when he does not know me and I do not know him? What token shall I give him so that he will recognize me, trust me, and give me the money? And I do not know the roads of Media to get there."

**5:3** Tobit answered his son Tobias: "He gave me a promissory note and I gave him one; I split it in two and we each kept one half. I put my half with the money. And it has been twenty years since I deposited that money. So now, my son, find yourself a trustworthy man to travel with you, and we will pay him wages when you return; then go and retrieve the money from Gabael."

**5:4** Tobias went out to find such a man, and there he found Raphael, who was an angel — but he did not know this.

**5:5** He said to him, "Can you come with me to Rages in Media? Do you know the region there?"

**5:6** The angel said to him, "I can go with you; I know the region well, and I have stayed as a guest with our kinsman Gabael."

**5:7** Tobias said to him, "Wait here for me while I go tell my father."

**5:8** He went in and told his father: "Look — I have found a man from among our own brothers, one of the sons of Israel."

Tobit said, "Call him in to me, so that I may learn what tribe he is from and whether he is a trustworthy companion."

**5:9** Tobias went out and called him: "Young man, my father is asking for you."

He came in, and Tobit greeted him first. Raphael said, "May you have every joy."

Tobit replied: "What joy is there still for me? I am a blind man who cannot see the light of heaven. I dwell in darkness like the dead who see the light no more. I am a living dead man — I hear voices but I cannot see."

Raphael said to him, "Take heart; God's healing for you is close at hand. Take heart."

Tobit said, "My son Tobias wishes to travel to Media. Can you lead him and guide him on the way? I will pay you wages, brother."

He said, "I can go with him. I know the roads, and I have stayed with our kinsman Gabael who lives at Rages in Media. It is two days' journey from Ecbatana to Rages, for Rages lies in the hill country."

**5:10** Tobit said to him, "Tell me, brother — what tribe and family are you from?"

**5:11** He said, "What tribe are you looking for? What family?"

Tobit said, "I want to know, brother, what tribe you belong to and what your name is."

**5:12** He said, "I am Azariah, son of the great Ananias, one of your own kinsmen."

**5:13** Tobit said, "You are welcome here, brother! Do not be offended that I asked about your tribe and family — it turns out you are truly my brother, from a good and noble lineage. I knew Ananias and Nathan, the sons of the great Shemaiah. We used to journey to Jerusalem together to worship, offering the firstborn animals and the tithes of the produce. They were never led astray into the error of our brethren. You come from a great family, brother.

**5:14** But tell me: what wages shall I give you? A drachma a day, and what you need just as I provide for my own son?

**5:15** And if you return with him safely, I will add something extra to your wages."

And so they came to an agreement.

**5:16** Tobit said to Tobias: "My son, prepare yourself for the journey and set out with your brother. May God in heaven prosper your way and may his angel accompany you."

They both set out, and the young man's dog followed along behind them.

**5:17** His mother Hannah wept and said to Tobit: "Why have you sent my child away? Is he not the staff of our hands — does he not go in and out before us?

**5:18** Do not pile money upon money; let it serve as ransom for our child.

**5:19** For the life the Lord has given us is enough for us."

**5:20** Tobit said to her, "Do not worry, my sister. He will go out safely and return to us safely, and your own eyes will see him.

**5:21** For a good angel will accompany him, his journey will be blessed, and he will return safe."

Then she stopped weeping.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agreed on preserving the dramatic irony announcement at v. 4 ("but he did not know this"), recognizing it as a defining structural feature of the narrative. The dog at v. 16 was retained by all three as a significant Sinaiticus-specific detail. Tobit's lament at v. 9 drew genuine divergence in rendering the oxymoron *nekros zōn* (see Disagreement Log). Hannah's three-verse maternal lament (vv. 17–19) was preserved intact by all translators.

---
## Disagreement Log

| Verse | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA's Resolution |
|-------|------|-------|--------|---------------------|
| 5:3 | "note-of-hand" | "promissory note" | "promissory note" | "promissory note" — LOGOS/PNEUMA consensus; EMET's "note of hand" is archaic |
| 5:4 | "Raphael who-was an-angel; and he-did-not know [it]" | "Raphael the angel standing there — but he did not know that he was an angel" | "there was Raphael — an angel, though Tobias had no idea" | SOPHIA blend: "there he found Raphael, who was an angel — but he did not know this" |
| 5:8 | "I-have-found a-man from our-brethren, of-the sons of-Israel" | "I have found a man from our own brothers, one of the sons of Israel" | "I found someone! One of our own people, a son of Israel" | LOGOS — PNEUMA's exclamation mark adds excitement but breaks the narrative register |
| 5:9 | "Living-dead I-am" (oxymoron preserved) | "I am among the living dead" | "I'm a living corpse" | SOPHIA blend: "I am a living dead man" — preserves the paradox more directly than LOGOS, less visceral than PNEUMA |
| 5:12 | "Azariah, son of-the great Ananias" | "Azariah, the son of the great Ananias" | "I'm Azariah. Son of the great Ananias" | LOGOS — complete sentence, formal register |
| 5:13 | "Jathan, the-sons of-the great Shemaiah" | "Nathan, the sons of the great Shemaiah" | "Nathan, the sons of old Shemaiah" | LOGOS — "Nathan" as standard English form; "old" (PNEUMA) too informal for a family lineage claim |
| 5:14 | "A-drachma a-day and what-is-necessary for you just-as for my-son" | "A drachma a day, and what you need just as I provide for my own son" | "A drachma a day, plus expenses" | LOGOS — preserves the comparison to Tobias, which is humanizing and important |
| 5:15 | "if you-return whole" | "if you bring him back safely" | "if you bring him back safely" | LOGOS/PNEUMA consensus — "whole" (EMET) is too literal for natural reading |
| 5:17 | "Is-he-not the-staff of-our-hands" | "Is he not the staff of our hands" | "He's the one we lean on — he's our hands and feet!" | LOGOS — preserves the Hebrew idiom formally; PNEUMA's expansion loses the Semitic flavor |
| 5:18 | "Do-not add money to-money; let-it-be as-ransom for our-child" | "Do not heap money upon money; let it serve as ransom for our child" | "Don't put money above our child. Whatever it costs, let that money be the price for keeping him safe" | LOGOS — "heap money upon money" is precise; PNEUMA's expansion dilutes the tension of the line |
